decision: FALSIFIES per frozen decision_rule — C1 behavioral detection mean TN=0.667 < 0.85 threshold. The HS256 symmetric JWT fix resolved token cross-node validation (TP=1.0), but per-node SQLite session store does not replicate sessions across distributed nodes. Round-robin routing sends valid-token requests to a node lacking the originating session_id, causing validate_session()=False and behavioral_delta>0 for valid tokens on /api/session/status (TN=0.0 on that endpoint, 1.0 on the other two). This is a genuine distributed infrastructure limitation (session non-replication), not measurement error. Critically, the frozen correlation gate C3-C7 all PASS: stratified r=-0.038, CI upper=0.029 < 0.15, TOST p=2.0e-08, confound detection |r|=0.912, local regression |r|=0.058. Orthogonality correlation is confirmed on distributed infrastructure; C1 detection fidelity fails for session-dependent endpoints only. Director bounds claim ceiling narrower than frozen rule: C-FRESHNESS orthogonality correlation confirmed on distributed 2-node Flask HS256 with independent session stores; C1 gate fails for session-dependent endpoints under round-robin without session affinity.

claim_updates.reason: Orthogonality correlation strongly confirmed on distributed infrastructure (stratified r=-0.038, CI upper 0.029 < delta=0.15, TOST p=2.0e-08, n_non304=844, audit PASS on all correlation metrics). However, frozen C1-C7 gate fails on C1 only (TN=0.667 < 0.85): session-dependent endpoint /api/session/status has TN=0.0 because per-node SQLite session store does not replicate across round-robin nodes. TP=1.0 confirms token validation works with HS256. The correlation is sound but the detection fidelity gate fails for session endpoints; the claim remains EXPERIMENTAL until C1 passes on distributed infrastructure with session affinity or shared session store. Do not advance to VALIDATED or PRODUCT_CORE.

product_action: NO_PRODUCT_ACTION — orthogonality correlation confirmed (C3/C4 pass strongly) but C1 gate failure means parallel-channel architecture is NOT fully justified for multi-node deployment under stateless round-robin without session affinity. Product may proceed with sticky session affinity or externalized session store (Redis) to resolve session-dependent endpoint TN failure. The correlation evidence (r=-0.038, CI upper 0.029) supports that behavioral-structural channels are orthogonal under distribution; the C1 failure is architectural (session state), not correlational.
next_question: Does C-FRESHNESS achieve CONFIRMED status on distributed infrastructure when session affinity (sticky routing) or shared session store (Redis) is added to resolve the per-node SQLite session non-replication that causes C1 TN=0.0 on /api/session/status?

The C1 failure is attributable to a single architectural limitation — per-node session stores without replication under round-robin routing — not to behavioral-structural correlation. The HS256 fix successfully resolved the RSA key sharing bug (tokens valid across nodes, TP=1.0). The parent's MEASUREMENT_INVALID due to RSA bugs is now resolved; the data is valid but the C1 gate fails. The claim ceiling is bounded to: orthogonality correlation confirmed on distributed 2-node Flask HS256 with independent caches and independent session stores; C1 detection fidelity fails for session-dependent endpoints under round-robin without session affinity.
